label: Alcohol & drugs
title: Alcohol, drugs and driving
headline: Feeling fine isn't the same as being fine
intro: Alcohol, drugs and some medicines slow you down long before you feel it. See how risk rises, and what the law says.

topics.title: Alcohol
topics.blurb: How risk rises with every drink

scenes.question: A driver at a blood alcohol level of {n:0.08} g/dl is about how many times more likely to crash than a sober driver?

lines: It's Saturday. You've had a few beers at a friend's braai and you feel fine.
Home is only ten minutes away.

art.alt: A road at night, lit only by dipped headlights.

lines: Your car keys are in your pocket. Nobody would stop you.

art.alt: A beer bottle beside a car key.

scenes.title: Crash risk and blood alcohol
scenes.caption: The risk doesn't rise in a straight line: it climbs steeply after a few drinks. At {n:0.15} g/dl a driver is about {claim:int.bac.rr-015} more likely to crash.

scenes.explain: At {n:0.08} g/dl a driver is about {claim:int.bac.rr-008} more likely to crash than a sober one. Namibia's limit is {claim:na.law.bac-blood} of blood, and you can be charged with driving under the influence at any level.

questions.prompt: What's the maximum fine for drink-driving?
questions.reason: The maximum is a fine of {claim:na.law.dui-fine} or prison for up to {claim:na.law.dui-prison}, or both.

questions.prompt: After a first conviction, your licence is suspended for at least:
questions.reason: At least {claim:na.law.dui-suspend-1} after a first conviction, {claim:na.law.dui-suspend-2} after a second, and {claim:na.law.dui-suspend-3} after a third.

questions.prompt: You can refuse a breath test if you feel sober.
questions.reason: Refusing a breath or blood test without a health reason is an offence in itself.

art.alt: A beer bottle beside a car key.

questions.line: You're the designated driver, but your friends keep offering you drinks.

options.label: Stick to soft drinks all night
Have one, then wait an hour

questions.reason: There's no safe number of drinks or waiting time you can count on. Coffee doesn't sober you up.

bands.title: Worth knowing
bands.body: The penalties are heavy. Read the reasons again.

lines: If you drink, don't drive. Plan your way home before you start.
Feeling fine doesn't mean you're under the limit.
Never get in a car with a driver who has been drinking.

topics.title: Drugs and medicines
topics.blurb: Including the ones from a pharmacy

scenes.question: The risk of a fatal crash among people who have used amphetamines is about how many times higher?

lines: You've got a bad cold. The pharmacist gave you tablets and said they might make you drowsy.
You need to drive to work tomorrow morning.

art.alt: A blister pack of tablets beside a car key.

questions.prompt: Dagga (cannabis) doesn't affect your driving if you're used to it.
questions.reason: Cannabis affects attention, reaction time and your ability to judge distance and speed, whether or not you feel it.

questions.prompt: Which can make you drowsy or slow your reactions? Pick all that apply.
questions.reason: Many medicines, including some for allergies, sleep, pain, anxiety and depression, can cause drowsiness or slow reactions.

questions.line: You're not sure whether your new prescription affects driving.

options.label: Ask your doctor or pharmacist, and don't drive until you know

questions.reason: Ask a doctor or pharmacist. Driving under the influence of a drug with a narcotic effect is an offence, even if it was prescribed.

scenes.explain: People who have used amphetamines are about {claim:int.who.amphetamine} more likely to be in a fatal crash.

lines: If you take drugs, don't drive.
Read the label and ask your pharmacist whether a medicine affects driving.
If you feel drowsy, don't drive. Get a lift or wait.

scenes.title: The last round
scenes.label: A made-up story, based on common situations
scenes.warning: This story mentions a crash in which people were hurt. It doesn't describe the injuries in detail.
paragraphs: Petrus had driven home after parties before. He always felt fine.
That night he misjudged a bend outside Rundu and hit a car coming the other way. The other driver was badly hurt.
He lost his licence and his job as a delivery driver. 'I thought it was my risk to take,' he says. 'It wasn't. It was theirs too.'

signpost.text: If a crash has affected you or someone close to you, you don't have to deal with it alone. LifeLine/ChildLine Namibia offers free counselling: call {claim:na.support.lifeline}.
